properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured), RECURRENCE of flo2 F12: settled decisions still read "OPEN — …" in their NAME. The 2026-09-19 fix gave set_decision_status a `chose` field for the body and nothing for the name, and the prose-currency checks scan statement/description/decision/rationale but never `name`. The brainstorm skill writes the status INTO the name ("OPEN — does X…?"), which is a second, hand-kept copy of status that no settle act updates
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-29, item I3 of art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29.

① OBSERVED (flo2 design 50f966697d6c5024, reflow2 0.74.0). Six decisions settled with set_decision_status (status accepted, `chose` filled) still read "OPEN — …" in their names. Each needed a replace_text on `name`, echoing ~4–6 KB each, ~30 KB in all. NOT affected: the body. `chose` recorded the winner without re-sending it.

② PRECEDENT: flo2 F12 (2026-09-19) reported exactly this. Two decisions were settled correctly and left "still NAMED 'OPEN — is …?' with bodies ending 'Options, none chosen'" (quoted in tests/settling_a_decision_records_which_option_won.rs and the `chose` field's doc). req:settling-a-decision-records-which-option-won (accepted) and this capability (realized) answered with `chose`.

③ CANDIDATES.
(a) set_decision_status cannot change the name.
(b) Nothing notices a settled decision whose name still asks the question.
(c) The naming convention itself: the brainstorm skill tells the agent to name an exploratory decision "OPEN — does X…?", so status is copied into prose at birth.
(d) The observation is wrong: the names were rewritten and the reads were stale.

④⑤ MEASURED 2026-09-29.
· SetDecisionStatusReq (service.rs ~5748) has decision_id, status, approver, acted_at and chose, and NO name. (a) confirmed.
· prose_currency.rs:
  - PROSE_FIELDS = ["description","statement"];
  - GOVERNED_PROSE_FIELDS = ["statement","description","decision","rationale"].
  `name` is in neither, so settled_question_prose can never flag a stale name. (b) confirmed. This also bounds W2: the stale texts it did catch were bodies, not names.
· The served brainstorm skill, step 3: "name it as the open question (\"OPEN — does X…?\")". (c) confirmed.
· (d) refuted: the designer's six replace_text replies returned the old names before rewriting.

⑥ CLASS: status copied into a prose field at creation, with no act that moves both and no check that reads the copy. The 09-19 fix treated the body instance and left the name instance. The correct repair removes the copy or keeps it in step. Adding `name` to set_decision_status alone would leave every other status-bearing name ("PLANNED —", "SETTLED —" on epochs and decisions) open to the same drift.

⑦⑧ OWED. No pinning test and no fix. The test would assert that after set_decision_status(accepted), no read presents the decision under a name beginning "OPEN". Options for the fix are Anthony's (vocabulary):
- derive the status prefix at read time and store names without it;
- have the settle act rewrite a leading status word;
- add `name` to the scanned fields.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED. How many accepted decisions in reflow2's own design still carry an "OPEN —" name: not counted this triage.

CLOSED 2026-09-29, the CAUSE: fixed by reflow2 PR #623 (squash 449ba2b). Its change record, chg:a-settled-decisions-name-stops-asking, is in the committed design (main's export), not in this live store.

Verified in the merged code:
- set_decision_status takes `name` (tools/toolsnaps/set_decision_status.json), so a settle can retitle in the same call.
- prose_currency reads `name` beside the body, and the settle reply warns `name_still_reads_open`.
- A new gap sweep, settled_decision_named_open (detect.rs, name_leads_with_open), finds the ones already standing.
- It is pinned by crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_settled_decisions_name_stops_asking.rs (4 of 6 observed failing first).

THE INSTANCES STILL STAND, by design. The sweep, run on the branch's design, found 45 of 463 accepted decisions still named as open questions. None were renamed, because the names are the owner's records. They will surface as gaps once a server runs the new binary.
